cases.customer_question: Can I perform limited RF PHY testing just to verify test mode functionality instead of full RF testing?
question_variants: Do I need full RF PHY test for test mode verification?
Can partial RF tests confirm test mode?
Is 1M PHY testing enough for validation?
Can I reduce RF test scope for pre-check?
What is minimum RF test for test mode check?
cases.actual_issue: Determining minimum RF PHY testing required for pre-validation (test mode confirmation) versus full qualification.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Before full certification, you may want to check if your device can enter test mode and behaves correctly. You don’t always need to run every RF test for this early check—just a subset can be enough.
cases.consultant_answer: While full RF PHY testing includes multiple modes (1M, 2M, etc.), for the purpose of verifying test mode functionality and basic mandatory behavior, a reduced set of tests (e.g., 1M PHY subset) is sufficient. Full RF testing is only required for formal qualification reporting.
cases.decision_logic: Test scope can be reduced for internal validation; full coverage is only required for formal qualification submission.
cases.final_recommendation: Use a reduced RF PHY test subset (e.g., 1M mode) for test mode validation, and perform full RF testing later during formal qualification if required.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Relying only on partial tests for final qualification may lead to missing required RF coverage and failing certification.
